Orcs — Yrch

Les Orcs, appelés Yrch en sindarin, sont des créatures humanoïdes façonnées pour servir les puissances de l’Ombre. Ils apparaissent dès le Premier Âge dans les armées de Morgoth, puis deviennent les soldats les plus nombreux de Sauron et de ses lieutenants.

La Race Orcs représente leur héritage physique commun. Les différences entre tribus, lignées et créations successives seront portées par des Cultures distinctes, notamment Orcs communs et Uruk-hai.

Une origine incertaine

La nature exacte des premiers Orcs n’est jamais définitivement établie. Plusieurs traditions parlent d’Elfes capturés et corrompus ; d’autres évoquent des Hommes déformés, des êtres fabriqués par imitation ou plusieurs origines successives.

Morgoth ne pouvait créer une vie indépendante à partir de rien : il ne pouvait que corrompre et asservir. Les Orcs restent donc une parodie des Enfants d’Ilúvatar, capables de langage, de mémoire et de choix limités, mais issus de sociétés entièrement marquées par la domination.

Les serviteurs de Morgoth et de Sauron

Morgoth les utilisa comme soldats, mineurs, gardiens, pillards et esclaves. Après sa chute, plusieurs tribus se dispersèrent et vécurent sans maître unique.

Sauron rassembla et organisa de nombreuses tribus. Les Orcs du Mordor sont soumis directement à sa volonté, tandis que ceux des Monts Brumeux et des Montagnes Grises conservent davantage d’indépendance.

Apparence

Les Orcs communs sont courts, lourds et disproportionnés. Leur peau est épaisse, gris sombre ou noire, leurs jambes courtes, leurs bras longs, leur tête large et leur visage aplati. Les yeux sont souvent noirs ou brun rougeâtre et les crocs apparents.

Les variations tribales sont nombreuses. Cicatrices, brûlures, marques de fouet, tatouages, peintures et trophées servent à afficher rang, tribu ou survie à un châtiment.

Longévité et endurance

Leur durée de vie naturelle peut atteindre plusieurs siècles, mais peu dépassent cinquante ans en raison des guerres, rivalités, accidents et exécutions. Ils possèdent une endurance exceptionnelle et supportent marches forcées, faim, mauvais traitements, travail souterrain et manque de sommeil.

Résistances

Ils résistent remarquablement aux températures extrêmes. Cette adaptation leur permet de vivre dans les cavernes glacées, près des forges, dans les montagnes et dans les terres volcaniques du Mordor.

Sommeil et vision

Les Orcs communs dorment surtout durant le jour et peuvent rester actifs très longtemps avant d’avoir besoin d’un véritable sommeil. Ils voient parfaitement dans la pénombre et conservent une perception limitée même dans les ténèbres profondes.

Le Soleil et l’eau vive

La lumière naturelle du Soleil provoque douleur, fatigue, irritabilité et diminution de leurs capacités. Ils préfèrent les nuits couvertes, la fumée et les souterrains. Les Uruk-hai constituent une exception et peuvent agir librement en plein jour.

Les Orcs communs craignent aussi les eaux profondes et courantes, en raison de leur mauvaise aptitude à la nage, de leur équipement lourd et du caractère imprévisible des courants.

Tribus et société

Ils vivent dans des tribus, bandes ou garnisons. L’appartenance tribale détermine dialecte, marques, armes favorites, ennemis et territoires. Leur société respecte avant tout la puissance et la peur. Le pouvoir appartient à celui qui peut vaincre ses rivaux, distribuer le butin, punir les désobéissants et inspirer la terreur.

Violence, cannibalisme et enfance

La violence sert à établir la hiérarchie et maintenir la discipline. Coups, mutilations, privations, torture et exécutions sont courants. Le cannibalisme entre tribus peut servir à survivre, humilier un ennemi ou célébrer une victoire.

La reproduction et l’enfance sont souvent contrôlées par les chefs ou les maîtres de l’Ombre. Les jeunes apprennent très tôt à se battre, obéir aux plus forts, voler de la nourriture et craindre les chefs.

Femelles orcs

Les femelles sont peu visibles dans les récits de guerre, car elles vivent souvent dans les profondeurs des établissements. Elles participent pourtant à l’élevage des jeunes, à la préparation des aliments, aux réserves, au travail artisanal et à la défense des zones intérieures.

Nourriture et demeures

Ils sont omnivores et capables de consommer viande fraîche ou avariée, champignons, racines, animaux souterrains et provisions volées. Leurs établissements occupent cavernes, mines, tunnels, ruines et forteresses et comprennent dortoirs, forges, cages, fosses à nourriture, quartiers du chef et enclos pour Wargs.

Mines, artisanat et guérison

Les Orcs sont utilisés comme mineurs, terrassiers et bâtisseurs. Malgré leur apparence grossière, leurs forgerons peuvent être techniquement compétents : armes, armures, serrures, chaînes, pièges, machines de guerre et réparations rapides.

Leurs guérisseurs pratiquent cautérisation, sutures, remise en place des os, amputations, herbes puissantes et magie obscure, sans se soucier de la douleur ou des cicatrices.

Religion et Ombre

La plupart adorent les ténèbres et la puissance. Selon l’époque, ils peuvent honorer Morgoth, Sauron, le Roi-Sorcier, un Nazgûl, un Balrog ou un chef divinisé. Leur obéissance repose surtout sur la peur.

Ils rêvent parfois d’une vie sans maître, mais reproduisent généralement les structures de domination dans lesquelles ils furent élevés.

Tempérament et langage

Ils sont cruels, jaloux, soupçonneux, querelleurs, lâches devant une puissance écrasante et féroces lorsqu’ils dominent. Ils peuvent néanmoins manifester camaraderie de bande, humour noir, loyauté tribale et fierté artisanale.

Leur conversation est bruyante, moqueuse et remplie de menaces. Ils savent cependant planifier, négocier, mentir et exploiter les rapports de force.

Langues

Chaque tribu parle son propre dialecte orquien. Le Parler Noir sert à unifier les serviteurs de Sauron et est surtout maîtrisé par les officiers, prêtres et Uruk-hai. Ils apprennent aussi le westron et les langues des peuples qu’ils combattent.

Relations

Les tribus se méprisent et rivalisent pour les cavernes, réserves et faveurs du maître. Elles haïssent particulièrement les Elfes et les Nains, craignent les guerriers disciplinés des Hommes et utilisent loups et Wargs comme montures, gardiens et pisteurs.

Ils portent peaux, cuir, tissus volés, pièces d’armure et métal récupéré, décorés de dents, os, chaînes, symboles tribaux et trophées. Ils utilisent cuir, maille, écailles, plaques partielles et casques.

Leur arsenal comprend cimeterres, épées courtes, haches, marteaux, masses, lances, arcs, arbalètes, fouets, gourdins et armes à deux mains.

Ils préfèrent la supériorité numérique, l’obscurité, les embuscades et les positions fortifiées. Ils utilisent pièges, tirs, charges soudaines, encerclement, otages, poison, feu et bêtes de guerre. Leur moral dépend fortement de la présence du chef.

Ils ne sont pas stupides : ils savent construire, forger, organiser des patrouilles, creuser, soigner, espionner et employer la magie. Les chamans, guérisseurs, devins et sorciers occupent des fonctions importantes.

Les rôles courants sont Combattant, Roublard, Voleur, Laïc, chasseur, pisteur, artisan, mineur, guérisseur orc, chaman, soldat et chevaucheur de Warg.

Morgoth ne pouvait créer une vie indépendante à partir de rien : il ne pouvait que corrompre, mutiler ou asservir. Pour le jeu, leur origine peut rester volontairement mystérieuse. Les Orcs sont des êtres vivants capables de peur, de langage, de mémoire, de choix limités et de relations sociales, mais issus de sociétés profondément marquées par la domination, la violence et l’influence de l’Ombre.

Les femelles sont beaucoup moins visibles dans les récits de guerre, car elles vivent généralement dans les profondeurs des établissements, loin des patrouilles et des champs de bataille. Selon la tribu, certaines peuvent devenir guérisseuses, artisanes, gardiennes ou dirigeantes locales.

Les Orcs sont omnivores et peuvent consommer des aliments que la plupart des peuples jugeraient répugnants ou dangereux : viande fraîche ou avariée, champignons, tubercules, céréales grossières, insectes, racines, animaux souterrains et provisions volées. Les Orcs possèdent un humour cruel, fondé sur les insultes, les blessures, les humiliations et les mésaventures des autres. Leur conversation est bruyante, moqueuse, agressive et ponctuée de menaces. Ils sont néanmoins capables de planifier, négocier et mentir ; un Orc peut paraître grossier tout en étant parfaitement conscient des rapports de force et des faiblesses de ses interlocuteurs.

Orcs — Yrch

Orcs, called Yrch in Sindarin, are humanoid creatures shaped to serve the powers of the Shadow. They appear as early as the First Age in the armies of Morgoth and later become the most numerous soldiers of Sauron and his lieutenants.

The Orcs Race represents their shared physical heritage. Differences between tribes, bloodlines and successive creations are expressed through distinct Cultures, especially Common Orcs and Uruk-hai.

An uncertain origin

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of Elves captured and corrupted; others of deformed Men, beings fashioned in imitation, or several successive origins.

Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt and enslave. Orcs therefore remain a parody of the Children of Ilúvatar, capable of language, memory and limited choice, but born into societies wholly marked by domination.

Servants of Morgoth and Sauron

Morgoth used them as soldiers, miners, guards, raiders and slaves. After his fall, many tribes scattered and lived without a single master.

Sauron gathered and organised many tribes. The Orcs of Mordor are directly subject to his will, while those of the Misty Mountains and Grey Mountains retain greater independence.

Appearance

Common Orcs are short, heavy and disproportionate. Their skin is thick, dark grey or black; their legs short, arms long, heads broad and faces flattened. Their eyes are often black or reddish-brown and their tusks visible.

Tribal variation is considerable. Scars, burns, whip marks, tattoos, paint and trophies display rank, tribe or survival of punishment.

Longevity and endurance

Their natural lifespan may extend for several centuries, but few live beyond fifty because of war, rivalry, accidents and executions. They possess exceptional endurance and withstand forced marches, hunger, abuse, underground labour and lack of sleep.

Resistances

They are remarkably resistant to extremes of temperature. This adaptation allows them to live in frozen caverns, near forges, in mountains and in the volcanic lands of Mordor.

Sleep and vision

Common Orcs sleep chiefly during the day and can remain active for a very long time before requiring true sleep. They see perfectly in dim light and retain limited perception even in deep darkness.

The Sun and running water

Natural sunlight causes pain, fatigue, irritability and reduced capability. They prefer overcast nights, smoke and underground places. Uruk-hai are an exception and can act freely in full daylight.

Common Orcs also fear deep, running water because of their poor swimming ability, heavy equipment and the unpredictability of currents.

Tribes and society

They live in tribes, bands or garrisons. Tribal membership determines dialect, markings, favoured weapons, enemies and territories. Their society respects power and fear above all else. Authority belongs to whoever can defeat rivals, distribute loot, punish the disobedient and inspire terror.

Violence, cannibalism and childhood

Violence establishes hierarchy and maintains discipline. Beatings, mutilation, deprivation, torture and execution are common. Cannibalism between tribes may serve survival, the humiliation of an enemy or the celebration of victory.

Reproduction and childhood are often controlled by chiefs or masters of the Shadow. The young learn very early to fight, obey the strong, steal food and fear leaders.

Orc females

Females are little seen in tales of war because they often live in the depths of settlements. They nevertheless take part in raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, craftwork and defending inner areas.

Food and dwellings

They are omnivorous and capable of eating fresh or rotten meat, fungi, roots, underground animals and stolen provisions. Their settlements occupy caverns, mines, tunnels, ruins and fortresses and include sleeping chambers, forges, cages, food pits, the chief's quarters and enclosures for Wargs.

Mines, craft and healing

Orcs are used as miners, earthworkers and builders. Despite their crude appearance, their smiths can be technically competent, producing weapons, armour, locks, chains, traps, war machines and rapid repairs.

Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, with little concern for pain or scarring.

Religion and the Shadow

Apparence

Les Orcs communs sont courts, lourds et disproportionnés. Leur peau est épaisse, gris sombre ou noire, leurs jambes courtes, leurs bras longs, leur tête large et leur visage aplati. Les yeux sont souvent noirs ou brun rougeâtre et les crocs apparents.

Longévité et endurance

Ils résistent remarquablement aux températures extrêmes. Cette adaptation leur permet de vivre dans les cavernes glacées, près des forges, dans les montagnes et dans les terres volcaniques du Mordor.

Sommeil et vision

Les Orcs communs dorment surtout durant le jour et peuvent rester actifs très longtemps avant d’avoir besoin d’un véritable sommeil. Ils voient parfaitement dans la pénombre et conservent une perception limitée même dans les ténèbres profondes.

Orcs — Yrch

Orcs, called Yrch in Sindarin, are humanoid creatures shaped to serve the powers of the Shadow. They appear as early as the First Age in the armies of Morgoth and later become the most numerous soldiers of Sauron and his lieutenants.

The Orcs Race represents their shared physical heritage. Differences between tribes, bloodlines and successive creations are expressed through distinct Cultures, especially Common Orcs and Uruk-hai.

An uncertain origin

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of Elves captured and corrupted; others of deformed Men, beings fashioned in imitation, or several successive origins.

Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt and enslave. Orcs therefore remain a parody of the Children of Ilúvatar, capable of language, memory and limited choice, but born into societies wholly marked by domination.

Servants of Morgoth and Sauron

Morgoth used them as soldiers, miners, guards, raiders and slaves. After his fall, many tribes scattered and lived without a single master.

Sauron gathered and organised many tribes. The Orcs of Mordor are directly subject to his will, while those of the Misty Mountains and Grey Mountains retain greater independence.

Appearance

Longevity and endurance

Resistances

They are remarkably resistant to extremes of temperature. This adaptation allows them to live in frozen caverns, near forges, in mountains and in the volcanic lands of Mordor.

Natural sunlight causes pain, fatigue, irritability and reduced capability. They prefer overcast nights, smoke and underground places. Uruk-hai are an exception and can act freely in full daylight.

They live in tribes, bands or garrisons. Tribal membership determines dialect, markings, favoured weapons, enemies and territories. Their society respects power and fear above all else. Authority belongs to whoever can defeat rivals, distribute loot, punish the disobedient and inspire terror.

Violence establishes hierarchy and maintains discipline. Beatings, mutilation, deprivation, torture and execution are common. Cannibalism between tribes may serve survival, the humiliation of an enemy or the celebration of victory.

Reproduction and childhood are often controlled by chiefs or masters of the Shadow. The young learn very early to fight, obey the strong, steal food and fear leaders.

Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, with little concern for pain or scarring.

Most worship darkness and power. Depending on the age, they may honour Morgoth, Sauron, the Witch-king, a Nazgûl, a Balrog or a deified chief. Their obedience rests chiefly on fear.

They sometimes dream of life without a master, but generally reproduce the structures of domination in which they were raised.

Temperament and speech

They are cruel, jealous, suspicious, quarrelsome, cowardly before overwhelming power and ferocious when they dominate. They can nevertheless show gang camaraderie, black humour, tribal loyalty and pride in their craft.

Their conversation is loud, mocking and filled with threats. They are nevertheless capable of planning, bargaining, lying and exploiting balances of power.

Languages

Each tribe speaks its own Orcish dialect. The Black Speech is used to unify Sauron's servants and is chiefly mastered by officers, priests and Uruk-hai. They also learn Westron and the languages of the peoples they fight.

Tribes despise one another and compete for caverns, supplies and the favour of their master. They especially hate Elves and Dwarves, fear disciplined human warriors and use wolves and Wargs as mounts, guards and trackers.

They wear hides, leather, stolen cloth, pieces of armour and salvaged metal, decorated with teeth, bones, chains, tribal symbols and trophies. They use leather, mail, scale, partial plate and helmets.

Their arsenal includes scimitars, short swords, axes, hammers, maces, spears, bows, crossbows, whips, clubs and two-handed weapons.

They prefer superiority in numbers, darkness, ambushes and fortified positions. They use traps, missile fire, sudden charges, encirclement, hostages, poison, fire and war beasts. Their morale depends heavily on the presence of their chief.

An uncertain origin

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of Elves captured and corrupted; others of deformed Men, beings fashioned in imitation, or several successive origins.

Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt and enslave. Orcs therefore remain a parody of the Children of Ilúvatar, capable of language, memory and limited choice, but born into societies wholly marked by domination.

Servants of Morgoth and Sauron

Morgoth used them as soldiers, miners, guards, raiders and slaves. After his fall, many tribes scattered and lived without a single master.

Sauron gathered and organised many tribes. The Orcs of Mordor are directly subject to his will, while those of the Misty Mountains and Grey Mountains retain greater independence.

Appearance

Common Orcs are short, heavy and disproportionate. Their skin is thick, dark grey or black; their legs short, arms long, heads broad and faces flattened. Their eyes are often black or reddish-brown and their tusks visible.

Longevity and endurance

Their natural lifespan may extend for several centuries, but few live beyond fifty because of war, rivalry, accidents and executions. They possess exceptional endurance and withstand forced marches, hunger, abuse, underground labour and lack of sleep.

Resistances

They are remarkably resistant to extremes of temperature. This adaptation allows them to live in frozen caverns, near forges, in mountains and in the volcanic lands of Mordor.

Sleep and vision

Common Orcs sleep chiefly during the day and can remain active for a very long time before requiring true sleep. They see perfectly in dim light and retain limited perception even in deep darkness.

Natural sunlight causes pain, fatigue, irritability and reduced capability. They prefer overcast nights, smoke and underground places. Uruk-hai are an exception and can act freely in full daylight.

They live in tribes, bands or garrisons. Tribal membership determines dialect, markings, favoured weapons, enemies and territories. Their society respects power and fear above all else. Authority belongs to whoever can defeat rivals, distribute loot, punish the disobedient and inspire terror.

Violence, cannibalism and childhood

Violence establishes hierarchy and maintains discipline. Beatings, mutilation, deprivation, torture and execution are common. Cannibalism between tribes may serve survival, the humiliation of an enemy or the celebration of victory.

Reproduction and childhood are often controlled by chiefs or masters of the Shadow. The young learn very early to fight, obey the strong, steal food and fear leaders.

Females are little seen in tales of war because they often live in the depths of settlements. They nevertheless take part in raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, craftwork and defending inner areas.

They are omnivorous and capable of eating fresh or rotten meat, fungi, roots, underground animals and stolen provisions. Their settlements occupy caverns, mines, tunnels, ruins and fortresses and include sleeping chambers, forges, cages, food pits, the chief's quarters and enclosures for Wargs.

Orcs are used as miners, earthworkers and builders. Despite their crude appearance, their smiths can be technically competent, producing weapons, armour, locks, chains, traps, war machines and rapid repairs.

Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, with little concern for pain or scarring.

Most worship darkness and power. Depending on the age, they may honour Morgoth, Sauron, the Witch-king, a Nazgûl, a Balrog or a deified chief. Their obedience rests chiefly on fear.

They sometimes dream of life without a master, but generally reproduce the structures of domination in which they were raised.

Temperament and speech

They are cruel, jealous, suspicious, quarrelsome, cowardly before overwhelming power and ferocious when they dominate. They can nevertheless show gang camaraderie, black humour, tribal loyalty and pride in their craft.

Their conversation is loud, mocking and filled with threats. They are nevertheless capable of planning, bargaining, lying and exploiting balances of power.

Each tribe speaks its own Orcish dialect. The Black Speech is used to unify Sauron's servants and is chiefly mastered by officers, priests and Uruk-hai. They also learn Westron and the languages of the peoples they fight.

Relations

Tribes despise one another and compete for caverns, supplies and the favour of their master. They especially hate Elves and Dwarves, fear disciplined human warriors and use wolves and Wargs as mounts, guards and trackers.

They wear hides, leather, stolen cloth, pieces of armour and salvaged metal, decorated with teeth, bones, chains, tribal symbols and trophies. They use leather, mail, scale, partial plate and helmets.

They prefer superiority in numbers, darkness, ambushes and fortified positions. They use traps, missile fire, sudden charges, encirclement, hostages, poison, fire and war beasts. Their morale depends heavily on the presence of their chief.

They are nevertheless capable of planning, negotiating and lying; an Orc may appear coarse while remaining perfectly aware of balances of power and the weaknesses of those around him.

The Orcs — Yrch Race is available during all four Ages and should remain Restricted. The player should specify the tribe, place of origin, master or former master, reason for departure, relationship with sunlight, languages and the limits of the character's loyalty to the Shadow.

Femelles orcs

Leurs guérisseurs pratiquent cautérisation, sutures, remise en place des os, amputations, herbes puissantes et magie obscure, sans se soucier de la douleur ou des cicatrices.

Leur conversation est bruyante, moqueuse et remplie de menaces. Ils savent cependant planifier, négocier, mentir et exploiter les rapports de force.

Langues

Relations

Manière de combattre

Intelligence, magie et professions

Ils ne sont pas stupides : ils savent construire, forger, organiser des patrouilles, creuser, soigner, espionner et employer la magie. Les chamans, guérisseurs, devins et sorciers occupent des fonctions importantes.

Place dans la création de personnage

Orcs — Yrch

Orcs, called Yrch in Sindarin, are humanoid creatures shaped to serve the powers of the Shadow. They appear as early as the First Age in the armies of Morgoth and later become the most numerous soldiers of Sauron and his lieutenants.

The Orcs Race represents their shared physical heritage. Differences between tribes, bloodlines and successive creations are expressed through distinct Cultures, especially Common Orcs and Uruk-hai.

An uncertain origin

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of Elves captured and corrupted; others of deformed Men, beings fashioned in imitation, or several successive origins.

Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt and enslave. Orcs therefore remain a parody of the Children of Ilúvatar, capable of language, memory and limited choice, but born into societies wholly marked by domination.

Servants of Morgoth and Sauron

Morgoth used them as soldiers, miners, guards, raiders and slaves. After his fall, many tribes scattered and lived without a single master.

Sauron gathered and organised many tribes. The Orcs of Mordor are directly subject to his will, while those of the Misty Mountains and Grey Mountains retain greater independence.

Appearance

Common Orcs are short, heavy and disproportionate. Their skin is thick, dark grey or black; their legs short, arms long, heads broad and faces flattened. Their eyes are often black or reddish-brown and their tusks visible.

Tribal variation is considerable. Scars, burns, whip marks, tattoos, paint and trophies display rank, tribe or survival of punishment.

Longevity and endurance

Their natural lifespan may extend for several centuries, but few live beyond fifty because of war, rivalry, accidents and executions. They possess exceptional endurance and withstand forced marches, hunger, abuse, underground labour and lack of sleep.

Resistances

They are remarkably resistant to extremes of temperature. This adaptation allows them to live in frozen caverns, near forges, in mountains and in the volcanic lands of Mordor.

Common Orcs sleep chiefly during the day and can remain active for a very long time before requiring true sleep. They see perfectly in dim light and retain limited perception even in deep darkness.

Natural sunlight causes pain, fatigue, irritability and reduced capability. They prefer overcast nights, smoke and underground places. Uruk-hai are an exception and can act freely in full daylight.

Common Orcs also fear deep, running water because of their poor swimming ability, heavy equipment and the unpredictability of currents.

They live in tribes, bands or garrisons. Tribal membership determines dialect, markings, favoured weapons, enemies and territories. Their society respects power and fear above all else. Authority belongs to whoever can defeat rivals, distribute loot, punish the disobedient and inspire terror.

Violence, cannibalism and childhood

Violence establishes hierarchy and maintains discipline. Beatings, mutilation, deprivation, torture and execution are common. Cannibalism between tribes may serve survival, the humiliation of an enemy or the celebration of victory.

Reproduction and childhood are often controlled by chiefs or masters of the Shadow. The young learn very early to fight, obey the strong, steal food and fear leaders.

Females are little seen in tales of war because they often live in the depths of settlements. They nevertheless take part in raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, craftwork and defending inner areas.

They are omnivorous and capable of eating fresh or rotten meat, fungi, roots, underground animals and stolen provisions. Their settlements occupy caverns, mines, tunnels, ruins and fortresses and include sleeping chambers, forges, cages, food pits, the chief's quarters and enclosures for Wargs.

Mines, craft and healing

Orcs are used as miners, earthworkers and builders. Despite their crude appearance, their smiths can be technically competent, producing weapons, armour, locks, chains, traps, war machines and rapid repairs.

Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, with little concern for pain or scarring.

Religion and the Shadow

Most worship darkness and power. Depending on the age, they may honour Morgoth, Sauron, the Witch-king, a Nazgûl, a Balrog or a deified chief. Their obedience rests chiefly on fear.

They sometimes dream of life without a master, but generally reproduce the structures of domination in which they were raised.

Temperament and speech

They are cruel, jealous, suspicious, quarrelsome, cowardly before overwhelming power and ferocious when they dominate. They can nevertheless show gang camaraderie, black humour, tribal loyalty and pride in their craft.

Their conversation is loud, mocking and filled with threats. They are nevertheless capable of planning, bargaining, lying and exploiting balances of power.

Languages

Each tribe speaks its own Orcish dialect. The Black Speech is used to unify Sauron's servants and is chiefly mastered by officers, priests and Uruk-hai. They also learn Westron and the languages of the peoples they fight.

Relations

Tribes despise one another and compete for caverns, supplies and the favour of their master. They especially hate Elves and Dwarves, fear disciplined human warriors and use wolves and Wargs as mounts, guards and trackers.

Clothing, armour and weapons

They wear hides, leather, stolen cloth, pieces of armour and salvaged metal, decorated with teeth, bones, chains, tribal symbols and trophies. They use leather, mail, scale, partial plate and helmets.

Their arsenal includes scimitars, short swords, axes, hammers, maces, spears, bows, crossbows, whips, clubs and two-handed weapons.

Fighting style

They prefer superiority in numbers, darkness, ambushes and fortified positions. They use traps, missile fire, sudden charges, encirclement, hostages, poison, fire and war beasts. Their morale depends heavily on the presence of their chief.

Intelligence, magic and professions

They are not stupid: they know how to build, forge, organise patrols, excavate, heal, spy and use magic. Shamans, healers, seers and sorcerers occupy important roles.

Common roles include Fighter, Rogue, Thief, Layman, hunter, tracker, craftsman, miner, Orcish healer, shaman, soldier and Warg-rider.

Origin and moral condition

Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt, mutilate or enslave. For game purposes, their origin can deliberately remain mysterious. Orcs are living beings capable of fear, language, memory, limited choice and social relationships, but they come from societies profoundly marked by domination, violence and the influence of the Shadow.

Orc females

Females are far less visible in accounts of warfare because they generally live in the deeper parts of settlements, away from patrols and battlefields. Yet they participate in the survival of the community: raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, making clothing, tending the wounded, cultivating fungi, craftwork and defending inner areas. Depending on the tribe, some may become healers, craftswomen, guards or local leaders.

Food and storage

Orcs are omnivorous and can consume foods that most peoples would consider disgusting or dangerous: fresh or rotten meat, fungi, tubers, coarse grain, insects, roots, underground animals and stolen provisions. They generally prefer meat and strong drink. Storage is often unsanitary, but their constitution allows them to tolerate contaminated food better than Men.

Mines, craft and healers

Orcs are frequently used as miners, earthworkers and labourers. They enlarge caverns and build roads, tunnels, walls and fortifications. Despite their crude appearance, their smiths may be technically competent in forging weapons, armour, locks, chains, instruments of torture, mining tools, traps and mechanisms of war. Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, without concern for pain or the appearance of scars.

Humour and speech

Orcs possess a cruel humour based on insults, wounds, humiliation and the misfortunes of others. Their conversation is loud, mocking, aggressive and punctuated with threats. They are nevertheless capable of planning, negotiating and lying; an Orc may appear coarse while remaining perfectly aware of balances of power and the weaknesses of those around him.

Wargs and wolves

Orcs frequently raise, train or ally themselves with wolves and Wargs. These creatures serve as mounts, guards, trackers, hunters and war beasts. The relationship is rarely based on affection: intelligent Wargs bargain and may abandon the Orcs if battle turns against them, while ordinary wolves are controlled through hunger, beatings and training.

Place in character creation

The Orcs — Yrch Race is available during all four Ages and should remain Restricted. The player should specify the tribe, place of origin, master or former master, reason for departure, relationship with sunlight, languages and the limits of the character's loyalty to the Shadow.

Orcs — Yrch

Orcs, called Yrch in Sindarin, are humanoid creatures shaped to serve the powers of the Shadow. They appear as early as the First Age in the armies of Morgoth and later become the most numerous soldiers of Sauron and his lieutenants.

The Orcs Race represents their shared physical heritage. Differences between tribes, bloodlines and successive creations are expressed through distinct Cultures, especially Common Orcs and Uruk-hai.

An uncertain origin

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of Elves captured and corrupted; others of deformed Men, beings fashioned in imitation, or several successive origins.

Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt and enslave. Orcs therefore remain a parody of the Children of Ilúvatar, capable of language, memory and limited choice, but born into societies wholly marked by domination.

Servants of Morgoth and Sauron

Morgoth used them as soldiers, miners, guards, raiders and slaves. After his fall, many tribes scattered and lived without a single master.

Sauron gathered and organised many tribes. The Orcs of Mordor are directly subject to his will, while those of the Misty Mountains and Grey Mountains retain greater independence.

Appearance

Common Orcs are short, heavy and disproportionate. Their skin is thick, dark grey or black; their legs short, arms long, heads broad and faces flattened. Their eyes are often black or reddish-brown and their tusks visible.

Tribal variation is considerable. Scars, burns, whip marks, tattoos, paint and trophies display rank, tribe or survival of punishment.

Longevity and endurance

Their natural lifespan may extend for several centuries, but few live beyond fifty because of war, rivalry, accidents and executions. They possess exceptional endurance and withstand forced marches, hunger, abuse, underground labour and lack of sleep.

Resistances

They are remarkably resistant to extremes of temperature. This adaptation allows them to live in frozen caverns, near forges, in mountains and in the volcanic lands of Mordor.

Common Orcs sleep chiefly during the day and can remain active for a very long time before requiring true sleep. They see perfectly in dim light and retain limited perception even in deep darkness.

Natural sunlight causes pain, fatigue, irritability and reduced capability. They prefer overcast nights, smoke and underground places. Uruk-hai are an exception and can act freely in full daylight.

They live in tribes, bands or garrisons. Tribal membership determines dialect, markings, favoured weapons, enemies and territories. Their society respects power and fear above all else. Authority belongs to whoever can defeat rivals, distribute loot, punish the disobedient and inspire terror.

Violence, cannibalism and childhood

Violence establishes hierarchy and maintains discipline. Beatings, mutilation, deprivation, torture and execution are common. Cannibalism between tribes may serve survival, the humiliation of an enemy or the celebration of victory.

Reproduction and childhood are often controlled by chiefs or masters of the Shadow. The young learn very early to fight, obey the strong, steal food and fear leaders.

Orc females

Females are little seen in tales of war because they often live in the depths of settlements. They nevertheless take part in raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, craftwork and defending inner areas.

They are omnivorous and capable of eating fresh or rotten meat, fungi, roots, underground animals and stolen provisions. Their settlements occupy caverns, mines, tunnels, ruins and fortresses and include sleeping chambers, forges, cages, food pits, the chief's quarters and enclosures for Wargs.

Mines, craft and healing

Orcs are used as miners, earthworkers and builders. Despite their crude appearance, their smiths can be technically competent, producing weapons, armour, locks, chains, traps, war machines and rapid repairs.

Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, with little concern for pain or scarring.

Most worship darkness and power. Depending on the age, they may honour Morgoth, Sauron, the Witch-king, a Nazgûl, a Balrog or a deified chief. Their obedience rests chiefly on fear.

They sometimes dream of life without a master, but generally reproduce the structures of domination in which they were raised.

Temperament and speech

They are cruel, jealous, suspicious, quarrelsome, cowardly before overwhelming power and ferocious when they dominate. They can nevertheless show gang camaraderie, black humour, tribal loyalty and pride in their craft.

Their conversation is loud, mocking and filled with threats. They are nevertheless capable of planning, bargaining, lying and exploiting balances of power.

Languages

Each tribe speaks its own Orcish dialect. The Black Speech is used to unify Sauron's servants and is chiefly mastered by officers, priests and Uruk-hai. They also learn Westron and the languages of the peoples they fight.

Relations

Tribes despise one another and compete for caverns, supplies and the favour of their master. They especially hate Elves and Dwarves, fear disciplined human warriors and use wolves and Wargs as mounts, guards and trackers.

They wear hides, leather, stolen cloth, pieces of armour and salvaged metal, decorated with teeth, bones, chains, tribal symbols and trophies. They use leather, mail, scale, partial plate and helmets.

Their arsenal includes scimitars, short swords, axes, hammers, maces, spears, bows, crossbows, whips, clubs and two-handed weapons.

They prefer superiority in numbers, darkness, ambushes and fortified positions. They use traps, missile fire, sudden charges, encirclement, hostages, poison, fire and war beasts. Their morale depends heavily on the presence of their chief.

Intelligence, magic and professions

They are not stupid: they know how to build, forge, organise patrols, excavate, heal, spy and use magic. Shamans, healers, seers and sorcerers occupy important roles.

Common roles include Fighter, Rogue, Thief, Layman, hunter, tracker, craftsman, miner, Orcish healer, shaman, soldier and Warg-rider.

Origin and moral condition

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of captured and corrupted Elves, others of deformed Men or of several successive origins. Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt, mutilate or enslave. For game purposes, their origin can deliberately remain mysterious. Orcs are living beings capable of fear, language, memory, limited choice and social relationships, but they come from societies profoundly marked by domination, violence and the influence of the Shadow.

Orc females

Females are far less visible in accounts of warfare because they generally live in the deeper parts of settlements, away from patrols and battlefields. Yet they participate in the survival of the community: raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, making clothing, tending the wounded, cultivating fungi, craftwork and defending inner areas. Depending on the tribe, some may become healers, craftswomen, guards or local leaders.

Food and storage

Orcs are omnivorous and can consume foods that most peoples would consider disgusting or dangerous: fresh or rotten meat, fungi, tubers, coarse grain, insects, roots, underground animals and stolen provisions. They generally prefer meat and strong drink. Storage is often unsanitary, but their constitution allows them to tolerate contaminated food better than Men.

Mines, craft and healers

Orcs are frequently used as miners, earthworkers and labourers. They enlarge caverns and build roads, tunnels, walls and fortifications. Despite their crude appearance, their smiths may be technically competent in forging weapons, armour, locks, chains, instruments of torture, mining tools, traps and mechanisms of war. Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, without concern for pain or the appearance of scars.

Humour and speech

Orcs possess a cruel humour based on insults, wounds, humiliation and the misfortunes of others. Their conversation is loud, mocking, aggressive and punctuated with threats. They are nevertheless capable of planning, negotiating and lying; an Orc may appear coarse while remaining perfectly aware of balances of power and the weaknesses of those around him.

Wargs and wolves

Orcs frequently raise, train or ally themselves with wolves and Wargs. These creatures serve as mounts, guards, trackers, hunters and war beasts. The relationship is rarely based on affection: intelligent Wargs bargain and may abandon the Orcs if battle turns against them, while ordinary wolves are controlled through hunger, beatings and training.

Place in character creation

The Orcs — Yrch Race is available during all four Ages and should remain Restricted. The player should specify the tribe, place of origin, master or former master, reason for departure, relationship with sunlight, languages and the limits of the character's loyalty to the Shadow.

Orcs, called Yrch in Sindarin, are humanoid creatures shaped to serve the powers of the Shadow. They appear as early as the First Age in the armies of Morgoth and later become the most numerous soldiers of Sauron and his lieutenants.

An uncertain origin

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of Elves captured and corrupted; others of deformed Men, beings fashioned in imitation, or several successive origins.

Morgoth used them as soldiers, miners, guards, raiders and slaves. After his fall, many tribes scattered and lived without a single master.

They are not stupid: they know how to build, forge, organise patrols, excavate, heal, spy and use magic. Shamans, healers, seers and sorcerers occupy important roles.

Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt, mutilate or enslave. For game purposes, their origin can deliberately remain mysterious. Yet they participate in the survival of the community: raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, making clothing, tending the wounded, cultivating fungi, craftwork and defending inner areas. Depending on the tribe, some may become healers, craftswomen, guards or local leaders.

They generally prefer meat and strong drink. Storage is often unsanitary, but their constitution allows them to tolerate contaminated food better than Men.

Mines, craft and healers

Orcs are frequently used as miners, earthworkers and labourers. They enlarge caverns and build roads, tunnels, walls and fortifications. Despite their crude appearance, their smiths may be technically competent in forging weapons, armour, locks, chains, instruments of torture, mining tools, traps and mechanisms of war. Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, without concern for pain or the appearance of scars.

Humour and speech

Orcs possess a cruel humour based on insults, wounds, humiliation and the misfortunes of others. Their conversation is loud, mocking, aggressive and punctuated with threats. They are nevertheless capable of planning, negotiating and lying; an Orc may appear coarse while remaining perfectly aware of balances of power and the weaknesses of those around him.

Wargs and wolves

Orcs frequently raise, train or ally themselves with wolves and Wargs. These creatures serve as mounts, guards, trackers, hunters and war beasts. The relationship is rarely based on affection: intelligent Wargs bargain and may abandon the Orcs if battle turns against them, while ordinary wolves are controlled through hunger, beatings and training.

Place in character creation

The Orcs — Yrch Race is available during all four Ages and should remain Restricted. The player should specify the tribe, place of origin, master or former master, reason for departure, relationship with sunlight, languages and the limits of the character's loyalty to the Shadow.

Orcs — Yrch

Orcs, called Yrch in Sindarin, are humanoid creatures shaped to serve the powers of the Shadow. They appear as early as the First Age in the armies of Morgoth and later become the most numerous soldiers of Sauron and his lieutenants.

The Orcs Race represents their shared physical heritage. Differences between tribes, bloodlines and successive creations are expressed through distinct Cultures, especially Common Orcs and Uruk-hai.

An uncertain origin

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of Elves captured and corrupted; others of deformed Men, beings fashioned in imitation, or several successive origins.

Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt and enslave. Orcs therefore remain a parody of the Children of Ilúvatar, capable of language, memory and limited choice, but born into societies wholly marked by domination.

Servants of Morgoth and Sauron

Morgoth used them as soldiers, miners, guards, raiders and slaves. After his fall, many tribes scattered and lived without a single master.

Sauron gathered and organised many tribes. The Orcs of Mordor are directly subject to his will, while those of the Misty Mountains and Grey Mountains retain greater independence.

Appearance

Common Orcs are short, heavy and disproportionate. Their skin is thick, dark grey or black; their legs short, arms long, heads broad and faces flattened. Their eyes are often black or reddish-brown and their tusks visible.

Tribal variation is considerable. Scars, burns, whip marks, tattoos, paint and trophies display rank, tribe or survival of punishment.

Longevity and endurance

Their natural lifespan may extend for several centuries, but few live beyond fifty because of war, rivalry, accidents and executions. They possess exceptional endurance and withstand forced marches, hunger, abuse, underground labour and lack of sleep.

Resistances

They are remarkably resistant to extremes of temperature. This adaptation allows them to live in frozen caverns, near forges, in mountains and in the volcanic lands of Mordor.

Sleep and vision

Common Orcs sleep chiefly during the day and can remain active for a very long time before requiring true sleep. They see perfectly in dim light and retain limited perception even in deep darkness.

The Sun and running water

Natural sunlight causes pain, fatigue, irritability and reduced capability. They prefer overcast nights, smoke and underground places. Uruk-hai are an exception and can act freely in full daylight.

Common Orcs also fear deep, running water because of their poor swimming ability, heavy equipment and the unpredictability of currents.

Tribes and society

They live in tribes, bands or garrisons. Tribal membership determines dialect, markings, favoured weapons, enemies and territories. Their society respects power and fear above all else. Authority belongs to whoever can defeat rivals, distribute loot, punish the disobedient and inspire terror.

Violence, cannibalism and childhood

Violence establishes hierarchy and maintains discipline. Beatings, mutilation, deprivation, torture and execution are common. Cannibalism between tribes may serve survival, the humiliation of an enemy or the celebration of victory.

Reproduction and childhood are often controlled by chiefs or masters of the Shadow. The young learn very early to fight, obey the strong, steal food and fear leaders.

Orc females

Females are little seen in tales of war because they often live in the depths of settlements. They nevertheless take part in raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, craftwork and defending inner areas.

Food and dwellings

They are omnivorous and capable of eating fresh or rotten meat, fungi, roots, underground animals and stolen provisions. Their settlements occupy caverns, mines, tunnels, ruins and fortresses and include sleeping chambers, forges, cages, food pits, the chief's quarters and enclosures for Wargs.

Mines, craft and healing

Orcs are used as miners, earthworkers and builders. Despite their crude appearance, their smiths can be technically competent, producing weapons, armour, locks, chains, traps, war machines and rapid repairs.

Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, with little concern for pain or scarring.

Religion and the Shadow

Most worship darkness and power. Depending on the age, they may honour Morgoth, Sauron, the Witch-king, a Nazgûl, a Balrog or a deified chief. Their obedience rests chiefly on fear.

They sometimes dream of life without a master, but generally reproduce the structures of domination in which they were raised.

Temperament and speech

They are cruel, jealous, suspicious, quarrelsome, cowardly before overwhelming power and ferocious when they dominate. They can nevertheless show gang camaraderie, black humour, tribal loyalty and pride in their craft.

Their conversation is loud, mocking and filled with threats. They are nevertheless capable of planning, bargaining, lying and exploiting balances of power.

Languages

Each tribe speaks its own Orcish dialect. The Black Speech is used to unify Sauron's servants and is chiefly mastered by officers, priests and Uruk-hai. They also learn Westron and the languages of the peoples they fight.

Relations

Tribes despise one another and compete for caverns, supplies and the favour of their master. They especially hate Elves and Dwarves, fear disciplined human warriors and use wolves and Wargs as mounts, guards and trackers.

Clothing, armour and weapons

They wear hides, leather, stolen cloth, pieces of armour and salvaged metal, decorated with teeth, bones, chains, tribal symbols and trophies. They use leather, mail, scale, partial plate and helmets.

Their arsenal includes scimitars, short swords, axes, hammers, maces, spears, bows, crossbows, whips, clubs and two-handed weapons.

Fighting style

They prefer superiority in numbers, darkness, ambushes and fortified positions. They use traps, missile fire, sudden charges, encirclement, hostages, poison, fire and war beasts. Their morale depends heavily on the presence of their chief.

Intelligence, magic and professions

They are not stupid: they know how to build, forge, organise patrols, excavate, heal, spy and use magic. Shamans, healers, seers and sorcerers occupy important roles.

Common roles include Fighter, Rogue, Thief, Layman, hunter, tracker, craftsman, miner, Orcish healer, shaman, soldier and Warg-rider.

Origin and moral condition

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of captured and corrupted Elves, others of deformed Men or of several successive origins. Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt, mutilate or enslave. For game purposes, their origin can deliberately remain mysterious. Orcs are living beings capable of fear, language, memory, limited choice and social relationships, but they come from societies profoundly marked by domination, violence and the influence of the Shadow.

Females are far less visible in accounts of warfare because they generally live in the deeper parts of settlements, away from patrols and battlefields. Yet they participate in the survival of the community: raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, making clothing, tending the wounded, cultivating fungi, craftwork and defending inner areas. Depending on the tribe, some may become healers, craftswomen, guards or local leaders.

Food and storage

Orcs are omnivorous and can consume foods that most peoples would consider disgusting or dangerous: fresh or rotten meat, fungi, tubers, coarse grain, insects, roots, underground animals and stolen provisions. They generally prefer meat and strong drink. Storage is often unsanitary, but their constitution allows them to tolerate contaminated food better than Men.

Mines, craft and healers

Orcs are frequently used as miners, earthworkers and labourers. They enlarge caverns and build roads, tunnels, walls and fortifications. Despite their crude appearance, their smiths may be technically competent in forging weapons, armour, locks, chains, instruments of torture, mining tools, traps and mechanisms of war. Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, without concern for pain or the appearance of scars.

Humour and speech

Orcs possess a cruel humour based on insults, wounds, humiliation and the misfortunes of others. Their conversation is loud, mocking, aggressive and punctuated with threats. They are nevertheless capable of planning, negotiating and lying; an Orc may appear coarse while remaining perfectly aware of balances of power and the weaknesses of those around him.

Wargs and wolves

Orcs — Yrch

Orcs, called Yrch in Sindarin, are humanoid creatures shaped to serve the powers of the Shadow. They appear as early as the First Age in the armies of Morgoth and later become the most numerous soldiers of Sauron and his lieutenants.

The Orcs Race represents their shared physical heritage. Differences between tribes, bloodlines and successive creations are expressed through distinct Cultures, especially Common Orcs and Uruk-hai.

An uncertain origin

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of Elves captured and corrupted; others of deformed Men, beings fashioned in imitation, or several successive origins.

Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt and enslave. Orcs therefore remain a parody of the Children of Ilúvatar, capable of language, memory and limited choice, but born into societies wholly marked by domination.

Servants of Morgoth and Sauron

Morgoth used them as soldiers, miners, guards, raiders and slaves. After his fall, many tribes scattered and lived without a single master.

Sauron gathered and organised many tribes. The Orcs of Mordor are directly subject to his will, while those of the Misty Mountains and Grey Mountains retain greater independence.

Appearance

Common Orcs are short, heavy and disproportionate. Their skin is thick, dark grey or black; their legs short, arms long, heads broad and faces flattened. Their eyes are often black or reddish-brown and their tusks visible.

Tribal variation is considerable. Scars, burns, whip marks, tattoos, paint and trophies display rank, tribe or survival of punishment.

Longevity and endurance

Their natural lifespan may extend for several centuries, but few live beyond fifty because of war, rivalry, accidents and executions. They possess exceptional endurance and withstand forced marches, hunger, abuse, underground labour and lack of sleep.

Resistances

They are remarkably resistant to extremes of temperature. This adaptation allows them to live in frozen caverns, near forges, in mountains and in the volcanic lands of Mordor.

Sleep and vision

Common Orcs sleep chiefly during the day and can remain active for a very long time before requiring true sleep. They see perfectly in dim light and retain limited perception even in deep darkness.

The Sun and running water

Natural sunlight causes pain, fatigue, irritability and reduced capability. They prefer overcast nights, smoke and underground places. Uruk-hai are an exception and can act freely in full daylight.

Common Orcs also fear deep, running water because of their poor swimming ability, heavy equipment and the unpredictability of currents.

Tribes and society

They live in tribes, bands or garrisons. Tribal membership determines dialect, markings, favoured weapons, enemies and territories. Their society respects power and fear above all else. Authority belongs to whoever can defeat rivals, distribute loot, punish the disobedient and inspire terror.

Violence, cannibalism and childhood

Violence establishes hierarchy and maintains discipline. Beatings, mutilation, deprivation, torture and execution are common. Cannibalism between tribes may serve survival, the humiliation of an enemy or the celebration of victory.

Reproduction and childhood are often controlled by chiefs or masters of the Shadow. The young learn very early to fight, obey the strong, steal food and fear leaders.

Orc females

Females are little seen in tales of war because they often live in the depths of settlements. They nevertheless take part in raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, craftwork and defending inner areas.

Food and dwellings

They are omnivorous and capable of eating fresh or rotten meat, fungi, roots, underground animals and stolen provisions. Their settlements occupy caverns, mines, tunnels, ruins and fortresses and include sleeping chambers, forges, cages, food pits, the chief's quarters and enclosures for Wargs.

La nature exacte des premiers Orcs n’est jamais définitivement établie. Plusieurs traditions parlent d’Elfes capturés et corrompus ; d’autres évoquent des Hommes déformés, des êtres fabriqués par imitation ou plusieurs origines successives.

Sauron rassembla et organisa de nombreuses tribus. Les Orcs du Mordor sont soumis directement à sa volonté, tandis que ceux des Monts Brumeux et des Montagnes Grises conservent davantage d’indépendance.

Apparence

Les Orcs communs sont courts, lourds et disproportionnés. Leur peau est épaisse, gris sombre ou noire, leurs jambes courtes, leurs bras longs, leur tête large et leur visage aplati. Les yeux sont souvent noirs ou brun rougeâtre et les crocs apparents.

Les variations tribales sont nombreuses. Cicatrices, brûlures, marques de fouet, tatouages, peintures et trophées servent à afficher rang, tribu ou survie à un châtiment.

Longévité et endurance

Leur durée de vie naturelle peut atteindre plusieurs siècles, mais peu dépassent cinquante ans en raison des guerres, rivalités, accidents et exécutions. Ils possèdent une endurance exceptionnelle et supportent marches forcées, faim, mauvais traitements, travail souterrain et manque de sommeil.

Résistances

Ils résistent remarquablement aux températures extrêmes. Cette adaptation leur permet de vivre dans les cavernes glacées, près des forges, dans les montagnes et dans les terres volcaniques du Mordor.

Sommeil et vision

Les Orcs communs dorment surtout durant le jour et peuvent rester actifs très longtemps avant d’avoir besoin d’un véritable sommeil. Ils voient parfaitement dans la pénombre et conservent une perception limitée même dans les ténèbres profondes.

La lumière naturelle du Soleil provoque douleur, fatigue, irritabilité et diminution de leurs capacités. Ils préfèrent les nuits couvertes, la fumée et les souterrains. Les Uruk-hai constituent une exception et peuvent agir librement en plein jour.

Ils vivent dans des tribus, bandes ou garnisons. L’appartenance tribale détermine dialecte, marques, armes favorites, ennemis et territoires. Leur société respecte avant tout la puissance et la peur. La violence sert à établir la hiérarchie et maintenir la discipline. Coups, mutilations, privations, torture et exécutions sont courants. Le cannibalisme entre tribus peut servir à survivre, humilier un ennemi ou célébrer une victoire.

Femelles orcs

Ils sont néanmoins capables de planifier, négocier et mentir ; un Orc peut paraître grossier tout en étant parfaitement conscient des rapports de force et des faiblesses de ses interlocuteurs.

Wargs et loups

Les Orcs élèvent, dressent ou s’allient fréquemment avec des loups et des Wargs. Ces créatures servent de montures, gardiens, pisteurs, chasseurs et bêtes de guerre. La relation repose rarement sur l’affection : les Wargs intelligents négocient et peuvent abandonner les Orcs si le combat tourne mal, tandis que les loups ordinaires sont maintenus par la faim, les coups et le dressage.

Place dans la création de personnage

La Race Orcs — Yrch est disponible durant les quatre Âges et doit rester Restreinte. Le joueur doit préciser la tribu, le lieu d’origine, le maître ou ancien maître, la raison du départ, le rapport au Soleil, les langues et les limites de sa loyauté envers l’Ombre.

Orcs — Yrch

Orcs, called Yrch in Sindarin, are humanoid creatures shaped to serve the powers of the Shadow. They appear as early as the First Age in the armies of Morgoth and later become the most numerous soldiers of Sauron and his lieutenants.

The Orcs Race represents their shared physical heritage. Differences between tribes, bloodlines and successive creations are expressed through distinct Cultures, especially Common Orcs and Uruk-hai.

An uncertain origin

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of Elves captured and corrupted; others of deformed Men, beings fashioned in imitation, or several successive origins.

Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt and enslave. Orcs therefore remain a parody of the Children of Ilúvatar, capable of language, memory and limited choice, but born into societies wholly marked by domination.

Servants of Morgoth and Sauron

Morgoth used them as soldiers, miners, guards, raiders and slaves. After his fall, many tribes scattered and lived without a single master.

Sauron gathered and organised many tribes. The Orcs of Mordor are directly subject to his will, while those of the Misty Mountains and Grey Mountains retain greater independence.

Appearance

Common Orcs are short, heavy and disproportionate. Their skin is thick, dark grey or black; their legs short, arms long, heads broad and faces flattened. Their eyes are often black or reddish-brown and their tusks visible.

Tribal variation is considerable. Scars, burns, whip marks, tattoos, paint and trophies display rank, tribe or survival of punishment.

Longevity and endurance

Their natural lifespan may extend for several centuries, but few live beyond fifty because of war, rivalry, accidents and executions. They possess exceptional endurance and withstand forced marches, hunger, abuse, underground labour and lack of sleep.

Resistances

They are remarkably resistant to extremes of temperature. This adaptation allows them to live in frozen caverns, near forges, in mountains and in the volcanic lands of Mordor.

Sleep and vision

Common Orcs sleep chiefly during the day and can remain active for a very long time before requiring true sleep. They see perfectly in dim light and retain limited perception even in deep darkness.

The Sun and running water

Natural sunlight causes pain, fatigue, irritability and reduced capability. They prefer overcast nights, smoke and underground places. Uruk-hai are an exception and can act freely in full daylight.

Common Orcs also fear deep, running water because of their poor swimming ability, heavy equipment and the unpredictability of currents.

Tribes and society

They live in tribes, bands or garrisons. Tribal membership determines dialect, markings, favoured weapons, enemies and territories. Their society respects power and fear above all else. Authority belongs to whoever can defeat rivals, distribute loot, punish the disobedient and inspire terror.

Violence, cannibalism and childhood

Violence establishes hierarchy and maintains discipline. Beatings, mutilation, deprivation, torture and execution are common. Cannibalism between tribes may serve survival, the humiliation of an enemy or the celebration of victory.

Reproduction and childhood are often controlled by chiefs or masters of the Shadow. The young learn very early to fight, obey the strong, steal food and fear leaders.

Orc females

Females are little seen in tales of war because they often live in the depths of settlements. They nevertheless take part in raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, craftwork and defending inner areas.

Food and dwellings

They are omnivorous and capable of eating fresh or rotten meat, fungi, roots, underground animals and stolen provisions. Their settlements occupy caverns, mines, tunnels, ruins and fortresses and include sleeping chambers, forges, cages, food pits, the chief's quarters and enclosures for Wargs.

Mines, craft and healing

Orcs are used as miners, earthworkers and builders. Despite their crude appearance, their smiths can be technically competent, producing weapons, armour, locks, chains, traps, war machines and rapid repairs.

Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, with little concern for pain or scarring.

Religion and the Shadow

Most worship darkness and power. Depending on the age, they may honour Morgoth, Sauron, the Witch-king, a Nazgûl, a Balrog or a deified chief. Their obedience rests chiefly on fear.

They sometimes dream of life without a master, but generally reproduce the structures of domination in which they were raised.

Temperament and speech

They are cruel, jealous, suspicious, quarrelsome, cowardly before overwhelming power and ferocious when they dominate. They can nevertheless show gang camaraderie, black humour, tribal loyalty and pride in their craft.

Their conversation is loud, mocking and filled with threats. They are nevertheless capable of planning, bargaining, lying and exploiting balances of power.

Languages

Each tribe speaks its own Orcish dialect. The Black Speech is used to unify Sauron's servants and is chiefly mastered by officers, priests and Uruk-hai. They also learn Westron and the languages of the peoples they fight.

Relations

Tribes despise one another and compete for caverns, supplies and the favour of their master. They especially hate Elves and Dwarves, fear disciplined human warriors and use wolves and Wargs as mounts, guards and trackers.

Clothing, armour and weapons

They wear hides, leather, stolen cloth, pieces of armour and salvaged metal, decorated with teeth, bones, chains, tribal symbols and trophies. They use leather, mail, scale, partial plate and helmets.

Their arsenal includes scimitars, short swords, axes, hammers, maces, spears, bows, crossbows, whips, clubs and two-handed weapons.

Fighting style

They prefer superiority in numbers, darkness, ambushes and fortified positions. They use traps, missile fire, sudden charges, encirclement, hostages, poison, fire and war beasts. Their morale depends heavily on the presence of their chief.

Intelligence, magic and professions

They are not stupid: they know how to build, forge, organise patrols, excavate, heal, spy and use magic. Shamans, healers, seers and sorcerers occupy important roles.

Common roles include Fighter, Rogue, Thief, Layman, hunter, tracker, craftsman, miner, Orcish healer, shaman, soldier and Warg-rider.

Origin and moral condition

The exact nature of the first Orcs is never definitively established. Some traditions speak of captured and corrupted Elves, others of deformed Men or of several successive origins. Morgoth could not create independent life from nothing: he could only corrupt, mutilate or enslave. For game purposes, their origin can deliberately remain mysterious. Orcs are living beings capable of fear, language, memory, limited choice and social relationships, but they come from societies profoundly marked by domination, violence and the influence of the Shadow.

Orc females

Females are far less visible in accounts of warfare because they generally live in the deeper parts of settlements, away from patrols and battlefields. Yet they participate in the survival of the community: raising the young, preparing food, maintaining stores, making clothing, tending the wounded, cultivating fungi, craftwork and defending inner areas. Depending on the tribe, some may become healers, craftswomen, guards or local leaders.

Food and storage

Orcs are omnivorous and can consume foods that most peoples would consider disgusting or dangerous: fresh or rotten meat, fungi, tubers, coarse grain, insects, roots, underground animals and stolen provisions. They generally prefer meat and strong drink. Storage is often unsanitary, but their constitution allows them to tolerate contaminated food better than Men.

Mines, craft and healers

Orcs are frequently used as miners, earthworkers and labourers. They enlarge caverns and build roads, tunnels, walls and fortifications. Despite their crude appearance, their smiths may be technically competent in forging weapons, armour, locks, chains, instruments of torture, mining tools, traps and mechanisms of war. Their healers practise cauterisation, suturing, setting bones, amputation, potent herbs and dark magic, without concern for pain or the appearance of scars.

Humour and speech

Orcs possess a cruel humour based on insults, wounds, humiliation and the misfortunes of others. Their conversation is loud, mocking, aggressive and punctuated with threats. They are nevertheless capable of planning, negotiating and lying; an Orc may appear coarse while remaining perfectly aware of balances of power and the weaknesses of those around him.

Wargs and wolves

Orcs frequently raise, train or ally themselves with wolves and Wargs. These creatures serve as mounts, guards, trackers, hunters and war beasts. The relationship is rarely based on affection: intelligent Wargs bargain and may abandon the Orcs if battle turns against them, while ordinary wolves are controlled through hunger, beatings and training.

Place in character creation

The Orcs — Yrch Race is available during all four Ages and should remain Restricted. The player should specify the tribe, place of origin, master or former master, reason for departure, relationship with sunlight, languages and the limits of the character's loyalty to the Shadow.
